About Us

QISG leverages Quanta’s comprehensive resources to deliver collaborative solutions for our partners' energy infrastructure needs. We use in-house talent, expertise and resources to plan, design, engineer, manage, conduct maintenance on and construct projects.

Our turnkey service capabilities provide our customers with efficiency, consistency, attention to detail and safe execution. The QISG team brings together Engineering, Safety, Quality, Material Procurement, QA/QC, Right-of-Way Acquisition, Scheduling, Environmental Planning, Permitting, Title and Land Management expertise that ensure outstanding results for our clients.

About This Role

Quanta Infrastructure Solutions Group (QISG) is a rapidly growing interdisciplinary engineering company within the Quanta Services (Quanta) family of companies. Quanta Services ranks #1 on the ENR 2024 Top 600 Specialty Contractors list, designing and building some of the largest infrastructure projects in North America. QISG is seeking project level GIS professionals interested in working to support large-scale engineering and construction projects throughout North America by providing GIS solutions to our engineers, project managers, construction partners and clients.

About This Role

A GIS Coordinator within QISG focuses on data capture and real-time reporting for project-related internal engineering support with deliverables that ultimately serve our clients on large-scale energy generation and transmission-related projects. Collaborating with an in-house, multi-disciplinary engineering and construction team — including civil, structural, geotechnical, construction management, and construction experts — a GIS Coordinator plays a crucial role in providing GIS solutions on projects; responsibilities include customizing solutions to best serve individual projects/programs, performing daily quality control over all project deliverables, and performing the geoprocessing/analysis steps necessary for successful delivery.

INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.

GENERAL INFORMATION

Project: AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay
Duty station: Asunción, Paraguay
Part-time/Full-time: Full-time
Number of Workdays Estimated: 75 days (From 23.09.2026 to 19.03.2027)
Consultant Level: Level 4

PROJECT BACKGROUND

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), through funding from the Climate Technology Accelerator Fund (CTAF), is implementing the project “AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay”. The project aims to strengthen climate resilience and renewable energy planning through the development and demonstration of an AI-enabled geospatial platform integrating satellite-derived renewable energy resource mapping, climate risk analytics, and decision-support tools.

Paraguay's electricity sector remains highly dependent on hydropower, which increases vulnerability to climate-induced droughts and hydrological variability. At the same time, the country has significant untapped solar and wind energy potential, particularly in the Chaco region. However, the lack of high-resolution geospatial information limits evidence-based planning and investment decision-making. The project will address this gap by generating solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability datasets and demonstrating an interoperable geospatial platform to support government institutions, academia, and other stakeholders in advancing the country’s renewable energy matrix diversification.

Key Objectives Include

Develop and validate high-resolution renewable energy and climate risk maps.
Support the deployment of a prototype web-based geospatial platform.
Strengthen institutional and technical capacity in the use of geospatial tools for climate and energy planning.
Support stakeholder engagement, validation, and scale-up planning.
Generate evidence for future replication and investment opportunities in Paraguay and the wider Gran Chaco region.

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The Geographic Information System (GIS) and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will provide technical support for the collection, processing, analysis, validation, visualization and reporting of geospatial data required for the implementation of the CTAF project.

The key tasks of this consultant position are as follows:

Collect, organize, and assess spatial datasets from government institutions and public sources.
Conduct GIS processing and spatial analysis using appropriate software and methodologies.
Develop and validate renewable energy resource mapping products, including geospatial analyses to support renewable energy planning and investment decision-making. Generate, analyze, and validate climate-risk layers, including drought and flood-related information, and develop decision-support products for national stakeholders. Prepare geospatial databases, metadata, and cartographic products.
Support testing and validation of spatial data integrated into the project platform.
Participate in stakeholder consultations, deliver training sessions, and technical meetings.
Contribute to the preparation of reports, presentations, and technical documentation.
Provide recommendations for data management, interoperability, and future scale-up of the platform.
Liaise with relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment of information generated and interoperability with the systems in place.
Serve as the national geospatial specialist and coordinate technical aspects with the consulting firm responsible for system deployment, ensuring the quality, consistency, and integration of geospatial datasets and analytical outputs.
Provide technical review and quality assurance of datasets, platform components, metadata, and interoperability mechanisms delivered by the consulting firm responsible for developing the platform.
Support validation of platform integration requirements and future interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM.

SCOPE OF WORK

The GIS and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will be part of the project implementation team and will work under the direct supervision of the CTAF Project Manager at GGGI Paraguay and in close coordination with national counterparts.

The consultancy is expected to deliver the following key results:

Geospatial Data Assessment and Coordination Report: Compile, review, organize and assess national geospatial datasets availability, quality, accessibility, and suitability related to renewable energy resources, climate risks, topography, infrastructure, and environmental information. Develop metadata catalogue and geospatial database inventory. Identify technical requirements and recommendations to facilitate interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM, and coordinate with consulting firm.
Technical Review and Validation of Climate and Renewable Energy GIS Dataset Package: Review and validate generation, processing, integration, quality control, accuracy, and validation of solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability layers. Support quality assurance and consistency checks of geospatial datasets developed under the project. Prepare technical documentation and metadata.
GIS Platform Support and Validation Report: Support data preparation, testing, visualization, validation, and demonstration of geospatial layers within the prototype web-GIS platform. Assess compliance with national data management requirements and interoperability standards. Review repository structures, metadata management procedures, and data-sharing mechanisms. Document validation results and recommendations for SIAM Integration.
Capacity Building and Final Technical Report: Deliver technical support for workshops and stakeholder consultations. Participate in technology-transfer activities conducted by the consulting firm. Support knowledge transfer and institutional capacity-building activities with designated MADES personnel. Review training materials, user guidance documents, lessons learned, and final consultancy report summarizing all activities undertaken during the consultancy.
The Consultant must integrate the comments of GGGI, and the technical focal points of other institutions involved, within 5 days after receiving the comments or requests for revision of the deliverables. All reports will be produced in Spanish and English and will follow GGGI's format requirements and will be submitted along with full raw data sets, research materials, minutes, interviews, and participant listings. Executive summaries will be delivered in English, and the final consolidated product of the consultancy must include a full English translation.

REPORTING ARRENGEMENTS

During the first week of assignment the consultant will define the reporting arrangements of the consultancy, in consultation with the national counterpart and the Project Manager. The consultant shall provide his/her own computer equipment and maintain access to ArcGIS Pro and any other software required to successfully perform the assignment.

Payments will be made against delivery of the products with prior approval from MADES, and approval from the GGGI Project Manager.

The consultant is expected to work in close coordination with MADES and other relevant institutions and may be required to work from MADES offices or other locations designated by the Project Manager.

Qualifications/Experience/Knowledge

Academic Qualifications

Master's degree in Geography, Geomatics, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Environmental Sciences, Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a related field; or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

Professional Experience

Minimum 5-8 years of professional experience (preferred 7) in GIS, spatial analysis, or geospatial data management.
Demonstrated participation in at least 5 projects involving geospatial analysis and mapping, preferably related to natural resources management, environmental monitoring, climate change, land use planning, energy, or infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience in at least 3 projects involving integration, management, or development of geospatial databases and metadata systems, remote sensing, Earth observation, or satellite imagery processing.
Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects involving climate risk analysis, environmental assessment, disaster risk management, or related fields.
Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects implemented with government institutions, international organizations, development partners, or public-sector entities.
Demonstrated experience in geospatial database management, metadata development, and spatial data governance, preparing technical maps, reports, and geospatial products for decision-making.
Experience working in Paraguay or in the Latin America and Caribbean region.

The Following Will Be Considered Assets

Experience in renewable energy resource assessment, solar and/or wind potential mapping, renewable energy suitability analysis, or GIS-based energy planning.
Experience in web-GIS platforms, spatial data portals, online dashboards, or geospatial visualization tools.
Experience delivering capacity-building, technical training, or knowledge-transfer activities related to GIS and remote sensing.
Experience using Google Earth Engine (GEE), Python, or other tools for geospatial analysis and remote sensing applications.

Skills and Knowledge

Strong analytical and cartographic skills.
Knowledge of spatial data management and metadata standards.
Demonstrated proficiency in ArcGIS Pro for geospatial analysis, geodatabase management, metadata development, and cartographic production.
Ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Strong report writing and presentation skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken, is a mandatory requirement, as the consultant will be required to conduct meetings, prepare deliverables, and communicate with international stakeholders in English.

Date to close is Korean Standard Time (KST). Applications submitted after the deadline will not be considered Application. Cover Letter, and CV must be sent in English. A consortium, or a firm may not be engaged for the individual consultant assignment.

Introduction:

About AWC:

AWC is a pragmatic global conservation leader, restoring landscapes and providing hope for Australian wildlife. Guided by science, AWC delivers measurable conservation impacts at scale to secure the future of our most endangered species.

At AWC we are inspired by the unparalleled richness of Australia’s wildlife and we are united by our determination to protect its unique animals and landscapes. It is our mission to effectively conserve all Australian wildlife and habitats and our vision is for a world where Australia’s biodiversity is valued and effectively conserved by an engaged community.

The delivery of AWC’s mission is highly reliant on all AWC working collaboratively with each other as a cohesive, engaged, collaborative, high performing group guided by strong, effective leaders.

AWC’s work is guided by the following values. At AWC, we are:

Accountable - taking ownership of our actions and outcomes
Informed - working together to acquire and apply evidence, knowledge and experience
Respectful - demonstrating care, recognition and integrity
Dedicated - committed to delivering effective outcomes, with resilience and tenacity
Innovative - applying creative thinking for effective solutions
Sustainable - delivering long-term financial and ecological viability.

About the role:

In south west Western Australia, AWC manages four wildlife sanctuaries: Karakamia and Paruna, in the Perth hills; Mt Gibson, in the northern wheatbelt; and Faure Island, in Shark Bay. AWC runs a nationally significant reintroduction program across these sanctuaries, with feral predator-free 'safe havens' established on Karakamia, Mt Gibson and Faure Island, supporting suites of locally extinct and threatened mammal species.

Spanning 131,812 hectares approximately 350 kilometres northeast of Perth, Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary sits at the intersection of two major botanical provinces within the Southwest Australia Biodiversity Hotspot, supporting an extraordinary diversity of flora and fauna. It is home to Australia's most ambitious mammal reintroduction program and holds the national record for the highest number of species ever restored to a single conservation site, with nine of the 10 species reintroduced into the 7,838-hectare feral predator-free area, the largest cat and fox-free area in mainland Western Australia.

Reporting to the Regional Ecologist, South West, the Wildlife Ecologist will contribute to the leadership of AWC’s science program in the region.

The Wildlife Ecologist will be responsible for the implementation of AWC’s science program at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, including managing and mentoring junior science staff on properties within their remit. The role has significant intellectual component, related to the design, analysis and reporting of elements of the science program, commensurate with the professional skills acquired in a PhD or equivalent. The role also has a substantial field work component.

The Wildlife Ecologist must be strongly motivated to make a substantial difference in nature conservation, contribute to the development of the private nature conservation sector, and be willing to help develop and promote AWC’s conservation model, with particular application to the social and environmental context of the region.

Key duties of the position:

Lead the development, implementation and reporting of the science program at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary. Work will also occur on other AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Provide expert input to the design and reporting of AWC’s science program at AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Work in an integrated way with AWC Operations staff to design and, as relevant, implement and report on conservation and land management strategies at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, and potentially other AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Work effectively with key stakeholders, including Indigenous groups, AWC partners, government agencies, recovery teams, the conservation sector and local communities, to develop AWC’s conservation science program at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, and potentially other AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Communicate AWC’s science program to stakeholders, the scientific community and the public through scientific publications, reports, presentations, participation in workshops, etc.
Assist with AWC’s fundraising activities.

Critical competencies:

A demonstrated commitment to wildlife conservation, evidenced through work, education and other relevant activities.
Advanced knowledge of the conservation of Australian wildlife and ecosystems including the nature and functioning of the Australian biota; major threats to native wildlife and their habitats; and how these threats can be mitigated. Ideally, you will have experience working with land managers to design applied conservation land management strategies.
Excellent ecological field and research skills including high level knowledge of the ecological literature; advanced knowledge of experimental design and sampling methods; strong skills in vertebrate ecology and sound skills in field ecology generally; advanced skills in statistical analysis of ecological data and the use of computer software packages relevant to the position.
Getting things done: you need well-developed planning and organisational skills, including a demonstrated ability to prioritise and execute a range of tasks in an effective manner.
Leadership: you need strong leadership and team-building skills, including the ability to manage and coordinate a team of staff and volunteers working in remote areas.
Collaboration: you need good relationship-building and collaborative skills to perform your role as part of a team of conservation ecologists. You must be willing to contribute your expertise, and learn from the skills and ideas of your colleagues. You must be willing to engage with the experience and world-view of a diverse range of stakeholders involved in conservation management including AWC Operations managers and other staff, AWC partners, Traditional Owners and the broader community.
Scientific communication skills: you will have a well-developed capacity to write and review scientific reports and publications, compose funding applications and reports, and communicate science and conservation messages to a general audience.
Financial management, paperwork and compliance: you will have the ability to deliver projects in a cost-effective manner and to manage financial resources, and to ensure contracted obligations are met, commensurate with the requirements of the position.
Resourcefulness: you will have the ability to improvise and ‘problem-solve’, developing practical solutions with limited resources.
Travel and time in the field: you must be willing to travel away from base and conduct field work to meet the requirements of the position.

Qualifications and Experience:

A PhD in ecology or a related discipline. In some cases, graduates lacking a PhD but with equivalent proficiency in applied conservation science as evidenced by a higher degree (e.g. Masters), combined with extensive relevant experience, may be suitable for appointment to this role.
Experience working in conservation or a related field.

Licenses, Certificates and/or Training:

A valid manual driver’s licence is essential. You will need to be competent in driving a 4WD in field conditions. Training in relevant competencies may be required.
Senior first aid certificate (remote certification - highly desirable).
Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check, or willingness to obtain.

PLEASE NOTE
: The successful candidate will be expected to live on-site, with accommodation provided at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, approximately four hours drive from Perth, WA. Work rosters are determined by agreement with the Regional Ecologist, and may provide for regular days off-site. The execution of tasks associated with the position will involve fieldwork in remote locations and can sometimes be away from an established field base, often in isolated locations working alone.

jobs.description:
North Bristol NHS Trust (NBT) and University Hospitals Bristol and Weston NHS Foundation Trust (UHBW) have merged as of 1st July 2026 to become Bristol NHS Foundation Trust. This creates an exciting future that brings together the best of both organisations. As a single, strong and sustainable organisation, we will not only be able to deliver better outcomes for our patients and fairer care for our population, but it will also provide greater opportunities for our people.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust recognise the value of a healthy work-life balance. When applying, speak to us about how we might be able to accommodate flexible working, so your work life fits around your home life.

We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian and minority ethnic candidates as they are under-represented within the Trust.

Our job adverts may close as soon as sufficient applications have been received. Considering this, if you are interested in this role, please do apply as soon as you can.

Generative artificial intelligence (AI) describes algorithms that can be used to produce new content, including audio, code, images, text, simulations, and videos. It is developing all the time and is now being used as a support mechanism for all kinds of content-based creations. Please note the use of AI is monitored and if applicants have used it then they are required to declare this.

Job Overview

The post holder will play a key role in the coordination of data for Southmead Hospital which is the Adult Major Trauma Centre (MTC) in the Severn Major Trauma Network. Ensuring that clinical information from patient records of all major trauma patients admitted to this MTC is extracted, interpreted, and submitted in line with national deadlines, guidance and requirements for the National Major Trauma Registry (NMTR). The MTC is part of the Severn Major Trauma Operational Delivery Network and therefore there is a supportive component to the extended Trauma Units and Children’s Major Trauma Centre which are within the Severn network.

This post may also require providing efficient and timely administrative duties to the Major Trauma Centre (MTC) Management team and Major Trauma Practitioners (MTPs).

Main duties of the job

Data and information

To ensure that all NMTR eligible patients’ details are entered and submitted before deadlines to ensure that the MTC is able to be eligible for Best Practice Tariffs.
Identification, using the NMTR inclusion criteria, of patients admitted to the Trust with major trauma injuries and subsequent completion of data submissions via electronic data collection and reporting system.
To interpret and consolidate information from multiple sources to ensure a complete and accurate patient records on the MTC database and NMTR.
To support the clinical team to identify all relevant major trauma episodes using various systems including Emergency Department admissions, transfers, etc. and inputting details onto the major trauma tracking database.
To examine patient records, extracting relevant information and investigating where necessary, following the patient pathway from injury to discharge.
To be aware of all aspects of the data set required and ensure completion of any missing data.
Identify and resolve any discrepancies in the data, escalating system errors or queries appropriately.
To liaise with other hospitals as necessary to retrieve required information.
To work closely with MTPs and external stakeholders to ensure accuracy of data.
Any other duties relating to the NMTR requirements.

Working for our organisation

North Bristol NHS Trust employs over 12,000 staff providing healthcare to the residents of Bristol, South Gloucestershire and North Somerset from our award-winning hospital building at Southmead. We are the regional Major Trauma Centre, and an internationally recognised centre of excellence in a range of services and major specialities. Our vision is that by enabling our teams to be the best that they can be, we will provide exceptional healthcare, personally delivered.

North Bristol NHS Trust values all people as individuals. We aim to be an anti-discriminatory organisation and are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We welcome applicants from all underrepresented groups.

GCSE English Language and Mathematics at Grade 4/C or above, or equivalent qualification
Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint
IT skills or qualifications to ECDL/RSA standard, or equivalent experience

Experience of working with electronic databases and information systems
Experience of working to deadlines and managing competing priorities

Experience of working within a multidisciplinary team environment

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Project Manager - CERCLA/RCRA
jobs.description:
Senior Environmental Project Manager

Job Summary

We are seeking a Senior Environmental Project Manager
to join a collaborative environmental consulting team based in Marietta, Ohio
.

This is a senior-level opportunity for an environmental professional with strong, hands-on experience managing CERCLA and/or RCRA Corrective Action projects
, including technical, regulatory, client-management, and project-leadership responsibilities.

The ideal candidate will bring approximately 8+ years of progressively increasing technical and regulatory responsibility
, along with current and active client relationships, business development experience, and demonstrated leadership in regulatory negotiations and environmental project management.

Candidates based in Ohio
are preferred. Candidates in nearby markets such as Louisville, Lexington, Indianapolis, or potentially Pittsburgh
may also be considered, provided they can regularly travel to Ohio client and project sites within approximately a half-day drive
.

Compensation

Target base salary: $125,000-$150,000
Maximum base salary: Approximately $170,000 for a highly qualified candidate
Travel: Approximately 10-20% on average, with travel potentially reaching 25%

Key Screening Criteria

Candidates Should Be Able To Demonstrate The Following

Progressive CERCLA/RCRA Technical & Regulatory Experience

Approximately 8 years of progressively increasing individual technical and regulatory responsibility and ownership
of RCRA Corrective Action and/or CERCLA
project planning and management.

Experience May Include

Authoring CERCLA and/or RCRA investigation plans and reports, both independently and as part of a team.
Environmental investigation and characterization.
Remedial evaluation and alternatives analysis.
Remedy selection.
Remedy implementation.
Operations and maintenance activities.
Regulatory interaction and project management.
Developing project objectives, work plans, schedules, and budgets.
Managing environmental projects from investigation through remediation and/or closure.
Location & Ability to Travel

The candidate must be located where they can realistically and consistently travel to Ohio client and project sites within approximately a half-day drive
.

Ohio-based candidates are preferred
, but candidates may also be considered from locations such as:

Louisville, KY
Lexington, KY
Indianapolis, IN
Pittsburgh, PA
Other nearby locations where regular travel to Ohio is practical

Long-distance commuting is not desirable. The position requires proactive interaction with client representatives located in and around Ohio.

Current Client Relationships & Business Development

The successful candidate must demonstrate direct, current, and active client relationships
and experience with business development.

This Includes The Ability To

Maintain and grow existing client relationships.
Develop additional work with existing clients.
Pursue new clients and project opportunities.
Participate in business development meetings.
Call on existing clients and established professional relationships.
Leverage the candidate's own established industry relationships to generate and expand business.
Identify opportunities to expand environmental consulting services.
Current CERCLA/RCRA Team Leadership

Candidates should demonstrate current and growing leadership responsibilities
involving regulatory negotiations and project direction under CERCLA and/or RCRA
.

Relevant Experience May Include

Regulatory negotiations.
Permit applications.
CERCLA ARAR analysis.
Development of task and project objectives.
Regulatory strategy and decision-making.
Leading technical and regulatory discussions with clients and agencies.
Direct oversight of project teams and technical staff.

Active, hands-on CERCLA and/or RCRA Corrective Action experience, current client relationships, and project leadership are paramount for this position.

Job Description

The organization provides engineering and environmental consulting services to industry, development, and government clients throughout the United States.

The Senior Environmental Project Manager will play a key role in identifying, developing, and managing environmental and engineering projects and proposals. The position will involve technical research and analysis, regulatory evaluation, project planning, field investigation oversight, laboratory analysis, client management, staff leadership, and business development.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to manage a diverse range of environmental projects involving regulatory analysis and decision-making, compliance assurance, environmental investigation, remediation, and problem-solving related to environmental protection.

Projects may involve returning impacted properties to productive and safe commercial, industrial, and/or residential use
.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Geology, Hydrogeology, or another relevant science field.
Master's degree preferred.
Minimum of 8 years of direct, practical experience with RCRA and/or CERCLA environmental investigation and remediation projects.
Demonstrated progressively increasing project management and technical responsibilities.
Strong understanding of EPA, CERCLA, and RCRA regulations.
Demonstrated experience interacting with regulators and managing regulatory requirements.
Current and active client relationships within the environmental consulting industry.
Demonstrated business development and client-development experience.
Experience expanding existing client accounts and pursuing new project opportunities.
Professional Geologist (PG) or Professional Engineer (PE) preferred.
Strong people, project, and client management skills.
Experience leading and mentoring junior and mid-level technical staff.
Strong commitment to safety and quality.
Knowledge of quantitative and technical analyses and related software.
Excellent written, verbal, and public-speaking communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and quality.
Excellent analytical, multitasking, judgment, and critical-thinking abilities.
Ability to work effectively both independently and within a team environment.
Ability and willingness to travel to client sites, project sites, and company offices.
Ability to traverse uneven terrain, climb stairs, and perform the physical activities required for both office and field work.
Reliable transportation and a valid driver's license in good standing.

Key Responsibilities

Identify, develop, and manage environmental and engineering consulting projects and proposals.
Manage CERCLA and/or RCRA Corrective Action projects from planning through investigation, evaluation, remediation, and operations/maintenance as applicable.
Perform complex technical and regulatory analyses.
Identify and manage project risks.
Conduct environmental research and analysis.
Plan, schedule, supervise, and manage field investigations and laboratory analyses.
Interpret environmental data and prepare technical reports.
Develop and maintain strong client relationships.
Participate in business development activities and pursue new clients.
Develop additional work within existing projects and client relationships.
Utilize established professional relationships to identify and develop new project opportunities.
Attend business development meetings with new and existing clients.
Participate in client meetings and proactively maintain relationships with client representatives in Ohio and surrounding markets.
Provide direct oversight and management of mid-level and junior staff assigned to projects.
Coach, mentor, and develop project team members.
Participate in interviewing and hiring technical staff.
Provide leadership during regulatory negotiations and interactions under CERCLA and/or RCRA.
Support regulatory activities including permit applications, CERCLA ARAR analysis, development of task objectives, and project objectives.
Supervise field activities and ensure compliance with project standards.
Manage subcontractors and other project resources.
Ensure sample and data collection, analyses, evaluation, and interpretation are completed accurately and in accordance with project objectives.
Manage multiple projects simultaneously within established budgets, schedules, and deadlines.
Prepare project progress reports and status presentations.
Lead meetings with clients, regulators, stakeholders, and project teams.
Prepare and manage change orders.
Track project budgets and schedules.
Ensure projects are completed and closed out according to requirements.
Coordinate with financial team members to ensure project invoicing, billing, and payment collection are properly completed.
Lead the preparation, organization, writing, and editing of technical reports, proposals, and other documents.
Coordinate with other offices and disciplines as needed.
Interface professionally with clients, regulators, contractors, subcontractors, project stakeholders, staff, supervisors, and other personnel.
Travel to Ohio client and project sites as required.
Support regional and local business development activities.
Report through the Marietta, OH office.
Perform other duties as requested.

Office & Location Expectations

The position is based through the Marietta, OH office
, but there is flexibility regarding the candidate's home location.

For an Ohio-based candidate, the anticipated office presence would be approximately a portion of one week per month during the initial year
, with additional flexibility based on coordination needs with team members and clients.

Candidates outside Ohio may be considered from nearby markets where regular travel to Ohio is practical.

The successful candidate should be comfortable with a role that combines:

Client meetings
Business development
Project-site visits
Regulatory interactions
Team leadership and mentoring
Technical/project management
Periodic in-office collaboration

Travel

Expected travel is approximately 10-20% on average
, with travel potentially reaching 25%
depending on project and client requirements.

The candidate must be able and willing to travel regularly to Ohio client and project sites
, generally within approximately a half-day drive
, as well as to other company offices and project locations when needed.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a senior environmental professional who combines deep technical CERCLA/RCRA experience with project management, regulatory leadership, client development, and business development capabilities
.

This is not simply a project-management position. The successful candidate should be able to demonstrate:

8+ years of progressive CERCLA and/or RCRA Corrective Action experience
Current, hands-on technical and regulatory involvement
Current and active client relationships
A proven ability to develop and grow business
Current leadership of environmental project teams
Experience working directly with regulators
Strong project ownership from planning through execution
Ability to mentor and develop technical staff
Ability to travel throughout Ohio and surrounding markets

Active, hands-on CERCLA and/or RCRA Corrective Action experience, current client contacts, and demonstrated project leadership are the most important qualifications for this position.

and stakeholder engagement skills

Want to make a positive difference to the future of people and our one shared home, the Earth? Working at WWF could be your opportunity of a lifetime.

All around the world, people are waking up to the devastating impacts of climate change and nature loss. The situation today is worse than the darkest predictions of just ten years ago, pushing billions of people to the edge and threatening lives and livelihoods. At WWF, we are facing our biggest crisis – and our biggest ever opportunity – to create a better future for people and nature. With over 60 years of experience and an active presence in more than 100 countries, we work to achieve both on-the-ground and global policy action, from protecting and restoring species and their habitats, to transforming markets and policies toward sustainability.

Our people come from hugely diverse backgrounds and with a variety of expertise, ranging from conservation science and advocacy to HR and finance. We welcome applications from anyone who believes they can help us tackle this enormous global challenge and drive the urgent conservation impact needed to restore our planet.

What We Do

We are an independent conservation organization, striving to sustain the natural world for the benefit of people and the ecosystem. From individuals and communities to businesses and governments, we are part of a growing global movement calling for bolder action on climate and nature, demanding that world leaders set nature on the path to recovery by 2030. WWF works to address the most dominant drivers of nature loss through system-wide changes in how food and energy are produced and consumed, and in how financial systems are structured. By implementing change in every country, we aim to drive visible and positive impacts on the ground, helping to restore nature in the most critical places around the world, from the Amazon to the Coral Triangle.

Engaging everyone means addressing the barriers to participation faced by some groups in society, including local communities. Conservation will only be sustainable if it is owned by, and benefits, local people. That’s why Indigenous Peoples and local communities must be at the centre of action on climate and nature. WWF is committed to using its resources and global network to support these communities in creating together the most effective solutions where they live.

Humanity is still in time, we have a clear pathway to solve this crisis. At WWF, we call on everyone to join the global movement, change how we live, and take action now.

INTRODUCTION TO GGGI

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI) is a treaty-based international, inter-governmental organization dedicated to supporting and promoting strong, inclusive and sustainable economic growth in developing countries and emerging economies. To learn more please visit about GGGI web page.

GENERAL INFORMATION

Project: AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay
Duty station: Asunción, Paraguay
Part-time/Full-time: Full-time
Number of Workdays Estimated: 75 days (From 23.09.2026 to 19.03.2027)
Consultant Level: Level 4

PROJECT BACKGROUND

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), through funding from the Climate Technology Accelerator Fund (CTAF), is implementing the project “AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay”. The project aims to strengthen climate resilience and renewable energy planning through the development and demonstration of an AI-enabled geospatial platform integrating satellite-derived renewable energy resource mapping, climate risk analytics, and decision-support tools.

Paraguay's electricity sector remains highly dependent on hydropower, which increases vulnerability to climate-induced droughts and hydrological variability. At the same time, the country has significant untapped solar and wind energy potential, particularly in the Chaco region. However, the lack of high-resolution geospatial information limits evidence-based planning and investment decision-making. The project will address this gap by generating solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability datasets and demonstrating an interoperable geospatial platform to support government institutions, academia, and other stakeholders in advancing the country’s renewable energy matrix diversification.

Key Objectives Include

Develop and validate high-resolution renewable energy and climate risk maps.
Support the deployment of a prototype web-based geospatial platform.
Strengthen institutional and technical capacity in the use of geospatial tools for climate and energy planning.
Support stakeholder engagement, validation, and scale-up planning.
Generate evidence for future replication and investment opportunities in Paraguay and the wider Gran Chaco region.

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The Geographic Information System (GIS) and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will provide technical support for the collection, processing, analysis, validation, visualization and reporting of geospatial data required for the implementation of the CTAF project.

The key tasks of this consultant position are as follows:

Collect, organize, and assess spatial datasets from government institutions and public sources.
Conduct GIS processing and spatial analysis using appropriate software and methodologies.
Develop and validate renewable energy resource mapping products, including geospatial analyses to support renewable energy planning and investment decision-making. Generate, analyze, and validate climate-risk layers, including drought and flood-related information, and develop decision-support products for national stakeholders. Prepare geospatial databases, metadata, and cartographic products.
Support testing and validation of spatial data integrated into the project platform.
Participate in stakeholder consultations, deliver training sessions, and technical meetings.
Contribute to the preparation of reports, presentations, and technical documentation.
Provide recommendations for data management, interoperability, and future scale-up of the platform.
Liaise with relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment of information generated and interoperability with the systems in place.
Serve as the national geospatial specialist and coordinate technical aspects with the consulting firm responsible for system deployment, ensuring the quality, consistency, and integration of geospatial datasets and analytical outputs.
Provide technical review and quality assurance of datasets, platform components, metadata, and interoperability mechanisms delivered by the consulting firm responsible for developing the platform.
Support validation of platform integration requirements and future interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM.

SCOPE OF WORK

The GIS and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will be part of the project implementation team and will work under the direct supervision of the CTAF Project Manager at GGGI Paraguay and in close coordination with national counterparts.

The consultancy is expected to deliver the following key results:

Geospatial Data Assessment and Coordination Report: Compile, review, organize and assess national geospatial datasets availability, quality, accessibility, and suitability related to renewable energy resources, climate risks, topography, infrastructure, and environmental information. Develop metadata catalogue and geospatial database inventory. Identify technical requirements and recommendations to facilitate interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM, and coordinate with consulting firm.
Technical Review and Validation of Climate and Renewable Energy GIS Dataset Package: Review and validate generation, processing, integration, quality control, accuracy, and validation of solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability layers. Support quality assurance and consistency checks of geospatial datasets developed under the project. Prepare technical documentation and metadata.
GIS Platform Support and Validation Report: Support data preparation, testing, visualization, validation, and demonstration of geospatial layers within the prototype web-GIS platform. Assess compliance with national data management requirements and interoperability standards. Review repository structures, metadata management procedures, and data-sharing mechanisms. Document validation results and recommendations for SIAM Integration.
Capacity Building and Final Technical Report: Deliver technical support for workshops and stakeholder consultations. Participate in technology-transfer activities conducted by the consulting firm. Support knowledge transfer and institutional capacity-building activities with designated MADES personnel. Review training materials, user guidance documents, lessons learned, and final consultancy report summarizing all activities undertaken during the consultancy.
The Consultant must integrate the comments of GGGI, and the technical focal points of other institutions involved, within 5 days after receiving the comments or requests for revision of the deliverables. All reports will be produced in Spanish and English and will follow GGGI's format requirements and will be submitted along with full raw data sets, research materials, minutes, interviews, and participant listings. Executive summaries will be delivered in English, and the final consolidated product of the consultancy must include a full English translation.

REPORTING ARRENGEMENTS

During the first week of assignment the consultant will define the reporting arrangements of the consultancy, in consultation with the national counterpart and the Project Manager. The consultant shall provide his/her own computer equipment and maintain access to ArcGIS Pro and any other software required to successfully perform the assignment.

Payments will be made against delivery of the products with prior approval from MADES, and approval from the GGGI Project Manager.

The consultant is expected to work in close coordination with MADES and other relevant institutions and may be required to work from MADES offices or other locations designated by the Project Manager.

Academic Qualifications

Master's degree in Geography, Geomatics, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Environmental Sciences, Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a related field; or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

Professional Experience

Minimum 5-8 years of professional experience (preferred 7) in GIS, spatial analysis, or geospatial data management.
Demonstrated participation in at least 5 projects involving geospatial analysis and mapping, preferably related to natural resources management, environmental monitoring, climate change, land use planning, energy, or infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience in at least 3 projects involving integration, management, or development of geospatial databases and metadata systems, remote sensing, Earth observation, or satellite imagery processing.

Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects implemented with government institutions, international organizations, development partners, or public-sector entities.

Introduction:

About AWC:

AWC is a pragmatic global conservation leader, restoring landscapes and providing hope for Australian wildlife. Guided by science, AWC delivers measurable conservation impacts at scale to secure the future of our most endangered species.

At AWC we are inspired by the unparalleled richness of Australia’s wildlife and we are united by our determination to protect its unique animals and landscapes. It is our mission to effectively conserve all Australian wildlife and habitats and our vision is for a world where Australia’s biodiversity is valued and effectively conserved by an engaged community.

The delivery of AWC’s mission is highly reliant on all AWC working collaboratively with each other as a cohesive, engaged, collaborative, high performing group guided by strong, effective leaders.

AWC’s work is guided by the following values. At AWC, we are:

Accountable - taking ownership of our actions and outcomes
Informed - working together to acquire and apply evidence, knowledge and experience
Respectful - demonstrating care, recognition and integrity
Dedicated - committed to delivering effective outcomes, with resilience and tenacity
Innovative - applying creative thinking for effective solutions
Sustainable - delivering long-term financial and ecological viability.

About the role:

In south west Western Australia, AWC manages four wildlife sanctuaries: Karakamia and Paruna, in the Perth hills; Mt Gibson, in the northern wheatbelt; and Faure Island, in Shark Bay. AWC runs a nationally significant reintroduction program across these sanctuaries, with feral predator-free 'safe havens' established on Karakamia, Mt Gibson and Faure Island, supporting suites of locally extinct and threatened mammal species.

Spanning 131,812 hectares approximately 350 kilometres northeast of Perth, Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary sits at the intersection of two major botanical provinces within the Southwest Australia Biodiversity Hotspot, supporting an extraordinary diversity of flora and fauna. It is home to Australia's most ambitious mammal reintroduction program and holds the national record for the highest number of species ever restored to a single conservation site, with nine of the 10 species reintroduced into the 7,838-hectare feral predator-free area, the largest cat and fox-free area in mainland Western Australia.

Reporting to the Regional Ecologist, South West, the Wildlife Ecologist will contribute to the leadership of AWC’s science program in the region.

The Wildlife Ecologist will be responsible for the implementation of AWC’s science program at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, including managing and mentoring junior science staff on properties within their remit. The role has significant intellectual component, related to the design, analysis and reporting of elements of the science program, commensurate with the professional skills acquired in a PhD or equivalent. The role also has a substantial field work component.

The Wildlife Ecologist must be strongly motivated to make a substantial difference in nature conservation, contribute to the development of the private nature conservation sector, and be willing to help develop and promote AWC’s conservation model, with particular application to the social and environmental context of the region.

Key duties of the position:

Lead the development, implementation and reporting of the science program at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary. Work will also occur on other AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Provide expert input to the design and reporting of AWC’s science program at AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Work in an integrated way with AWC Operations staff to design and, as relevant, implement and report on conservation and land management strategies at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, and potentially other AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Work effectively with key stakeholders, including Indigenous groups, AWC partners, government agencies, recovery teams, the conservation sector and local communities, to develop AWC’s conservation science program at Mt Gibson Wildlife Sanctuary, and potentially other AWC properties and partnership sites in the region, as delegated by the Regional Ecologist.
Communicate AWC’s science program to stakeholders, the scientific community and the public through scientific publications, reports, presentations, participation in workshops, etc.
Assist with AWC’s fundraising activities.

Critical competencies:

A demonstrated commitment to wildlife conservation, evidenced through work, education and other relevant activities.
Advanced knowledge of the conservation of Australian wildlife and ecosystems including the nature and functioning of the Australian biota; major threats to native wildlife and their habitats; and how these threats can be mitigated. Ideally, you will have experience working with land managers to design applied conservation land management strategies.
Excellent ecological field and research skills including high level knowledge of the ecological literature; advanced knowledge of experimental design and sampling methods; strong skills in vertebrate ecology and sound skills in field ecology generally; advanced skills in statistical analysis of ecological data and the use of computer software packages relevant to the position.
Getting things done: you need well-developed planning and organisational skills, including a demonstrated ability to prioritise and execute a range of tasks in an effective manner.

new_jobs.description:
Want to make a positive difference to the future of people and our one shared home, the Earth? Working at WWF could be your opportunity of a lifetime.

All around the world, people are waking up to the devastating impacts of climate change and nature loss. The situation today is worse than the darkest predictions of just ten years ago, pushing billions of people to the edge and threatening lives and livelihoods. At WWF, we are facing our biggest crisis – and our biggest ever opportunity – to create a better future for people and nature. With over 60 years of experience and an active presence in more than 100 countries, we work to achieve both on-the-ground and global policy action, from protecting and restoring species and their habitats, to transforming markets and policies toward sustainability.

Our people come from hugely diverse backgrounds and with a variety of expertise, ranging from conservation science and advocacy to HR and finance. We welcome applications from anyone who believes they can help us tackle this enormous global challenge and drive the urgent conservation impact needed to restore our planet.

What We Do

We are an independent conservation organization, striving to sustain the natural world for the benefit of people and the ecosystem. From individuals and communities to businesses and governments, we are part of a growing global movement calling for bolder action on climate and nature, demanding that world leaders set nature on the path to recovery by 2030. WWF works to address the most dominant drivers of nature loss through system-wide changes in how food and energy are produced and consumed, and in how financial systems are structured. By implementing change in every country, we aim to drive visible and positive impacts on the ground, helping to restore nature in the most critical places around the world, from the Amazon to the Coral Triangle.

Engaging everyone means addressing the barriers to participation faced by some groups in society, including local communities. Conservation will only be sustainable if it is owned by, and benefits, local people. That’s why Indigenous Peoples and local communities must be at the centre of action on climate and nature. WWF is committed to using its resources and global network to support these communities in creating together the most effective solutions where they live.

Humanity is still in time, we have a clear pathway to solve this crisis. At WWF, we call on everyone to join the global movement, change how we live, and take action now.

Job Description

TERMS OF REFERENCE

JOB TITLE:
Project Executant

PROJECT:
The East Usambara Restoration project (EURP) SUPERVISOR:
Forest Programme Coordinator

SUPERVISE:
Project Field Officer

DUTY STATION:
Korogwe

Forest Programme Coordinator and Water Towers Landscape Lead.

SUMMARY:
WWF Tanzania seeks to hire a Project Executant for the The East Usambara Restoration project (EURP) to be based in WWF Tanzania Dar es Salaam Office and Tanga with frequent travels to the project area Korogwe and Mkinga districts in Tanga region including. S/he will report to the WWF Tanzania Forest Program Coordinator.

BACKGROUND

The Water Towers is one of the three terrestrial landscapes in WWF Tanzania Conservation Strategic Plan (CSP – III, 2025-2030) priority areas. It covers the Eastern Arc Mountain and Eastern Africa coastal forests which are recognized by IUCN to host high biodiversity hotspots with high species endemism. The WTL harbours the globally known high biodiversity hotspots and centres of endemism. WTL is unique as it includes the largest sources of water in the country, critical for human wellbeing, wildlife and the national economy.

The East Usambara Restoration project (EURP) is a four-year program (mid 2022-mid 2026) to be implemented in the East Usambara coastal forests sub-landscape of the WTL aiming to use innovative and multiple landscape restoration approaches that enhance human wellbeing and wildlife. WWF Tanzania is therefore looking for a person with strong and proven experience in leading a complex multi stakeholder project in the context of nature conservation and contribute to increased ecosystem services and peoples’ livelihoods in order to successfully deliver desired outcomes of the project. Must also have proven community engagement experience in restoration projects.

MAIN FUNCTIONS

The Project Executant will work for the overall project coordination of the East Usambara Restoration project (EURP) including engagement with implementing partners. This position will essentially involve considerable interaction with partners in Central and Local Government, National Government Authorities, Private sectors, National and Local Civil society organizations (CSOs), Community Based Organizations (CBO’s), Research institutions and local communities.

The Project Executant will be the key resource person for implementing the project activities, developing annual work plans and technical progress reports, managing the project risk register, developing and regularly tracking budgets and expenditures for the timely and successful delivery of the project. He/she must have proven track record of working on international conservation organizations and very good analytical and communication skills. She/he should thrive in environments that are dynamic, fast paced, collegiate and ambitious, and should be able to demonstrate experience in working independently and solving complex problems in remote and challenging environments.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND SCOPE

Implements the above-named project and prepares monthly updates, quarterly and annual technical progress reports.
Development of project annual work plan, budget, fund advance request and concept notes
Ensure smooth cooperation with WWF Switzerland, other project staff and parties to accomplish project activities and goals.
Financial responsibility may include working within available budgets, managing field budget and allowances for stakeholders and partners.
Creation of high-quality field stories, data bases and undertakes project monitoring and evaluation in collaboration with the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer and the Communications

Officer.

Ensure compliance with WWF internal policies and external requirements.
Actively engage and supports proposal development for other projects within WTL
Under minimal supervision, makes independent decisions based on analysis, experience and judgment.
Responsible for his/her project performance management, through training and career development with the help from the WWF TCO Forest Coordinator, and responsible of ensuring performance management of the Field officer as well
Supervise and guide the field implementing partners including participating villages
Identifies and aligns with the core values of the WWF organization: Courage, Integrity, Respect and Collaboration
Undertakes any other assignment as assigned from time to time by the Forest Program Coordinator and WTL Lead.
Ensure the project adhere to WWF ESSF procedures developed for the WTL.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCES

Bachelor degree on Forestry, Natural Resource Management, Social Sciences, Environmental Science or any other related field. A Master degree can be an added advantage.
Five years relevant professional experience in natural resources management, forest landscape restoration and community-based conservation projects and experience in coordinating and facilitating trainings and meetings.
Strong knowledge and understanding of the Theory behind Forest Landscape Restoration, Climate Change and application of Nature-Based Solutions for impactful restoration and community benefits.
Understanding of and sensitivity towards, the culture, gender, religion, race, age and livelihoods context of rural coastal communities in Tanzania.
A proven ability to work effectively under minimum supervision, working in a team and willing to travel regularly and to stay for periods and to travel at short notice.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills and good oral and verbal communication skills in both Kiswahili and English, with an ability to develop strong relations with Government, local NGOs, CSO, private sectors and community partners.
Good inter-personal and teamwork skills, networking aptitude and ability to work in multicultural environment.
Very good command in English & excellent writing skills and the ability to prepare clear, concise reports.

WORKING RELATIONSHIPS
Internal: Working closely with the WWF TCO Forest Program Coordinator and the forest program team with regular interactions with the WWF TCO team.
External: Liaising with WWF Switzerland Team, other WWF Network staff as necessary, CSOs, Private sector, Government Authorities and Local Communities.

Responsibilities

Operate and maintain pressure washing equipment to clean infrastructure, equipment pads, utility boxes, conduit areas, and other field assets
Remove temporary utility locate markings (paint and chalk) from streets, sidewalks, curbs, and driveways following fiber construction
Perform landscape restoration including sod replacement, irrigation repair, grading, mulch, decorative rock, and edging
Perform hardscape restoration including pavers, concrete, gravel, fencing, gates, mailbox posts, and utility lids
Perform the removal, lifting, cutting, rolling, and temporary protection of existing turf to provide access for underground Service Drop installations and other construction activities.
Properly prepare and protect turf prior to construction to minimize damage and maintain the integrity of the existing turf system.
Reinstall and restore synthetic turf following completion of underground construction work.
Perform standard turf repairs, including repositioning, leveling, securing, and correcting minor cuts, separations, and displaced areas.
Ensure turf is properly aligned with surrounding areas and that seams, edges, transitions, and finished surfaces meet Cityside Fiber restoration standards.
Coordinate with Service Drop and Field Operations personnel to ensure turf restoration is completed after construction activities are finished.
Identify turf conditions or damage that exceed standard restoration capabilities and escalate to management when specialized repair or replacement is required.
Document completed turf restoration work with required photographs and work-order notes.
Ensure proper water usage and compliance with local environmental regulations
Follow safe chemical handling, equipment operation, and personal protective equipment (PPE) protocols at all times
Inspect equipment before and after use and report maintenance issues promptly
Complete daily work orders and site documentation accurately and on time
Coordinate with construction crews and supervisors to prioritize clean-up and restoration areas
Safely transport equipment, materials, and tools to and from job sites and manage daily routes effectively
Support facilities maintenance, fleet washing, warehouse organization, material deliveries, and inventory as needed
Work in various outdoor environments and weather conditions throughout the service area
Contribute to a culture of trust, integrity, and collaboration
Understand and uphold Cityside Fiber's core purpose and values and be passionate about what we do

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the position. Management reserves the right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities as business needs evolve.

High school diploma or equivalent
2+ years of experience in pressure washing, landscaping, hardscape/concrete, construction clean-up, or a related field
Ability to work outdoors and in various weather conditions
Ability to lift and move equipment (50+ lbs) and perform physically demanding tasks
Strong attention to detail and pride in maintaining clean, professional communities
Ability to work independently and manage daily routes effectively
Familiarity with standard safety protocols and procedures, and a commitment to working safely in the field
Valid California driver's license, good driving record, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance
Availability for occasional overtime and weekend work as construction schedules require
